title: How to open, scope and drive a design round

claims.text: Order-of-magnitude figures make a design arguable without measurement: a main memory reference at around 100 nanoseconds, a round trip within the same datacenter at around 500,000, a disk seek at around 10,000,000, and reading 1 megabyte sequentially from disk at around 30,000,000.

source.title: Jeffrey Dean, Large-Scale Distributed Systems at Google: Current Systems and Future Directions, keynote at LADIS 2009, October 2009 — the slide deck carrying Numbers Everyone Should Know

claims.text: A request that depends on many components inherits their worst case rather than their average: with a single server at a 99th percentile of one second, a fan-out to 100 servers sees a slow response more often than not, and at 2,000 servers even a one in ten thousand chance means 18% of requests exceed one second.

source.title: Jeffrey Dean and Luiz Andre Barroso, The tail at scale, Communications of the ACM 56(2):74-80, February 2013, doi 10.1145/2408776.2408794

claims.text: The relationship between items in a system, arrival rate and time in system holds independently of the arrival distribution, the service distribution and the service order, so a capacity claim can be checked without knowing any of them.

source.title: John D. C. Little, A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = lambda W, Operations Research 9(3):383-387, June 1961, doi 10.1287/opre.9.3.383

beats.broke: an open-ended design question has no correct answer and the failure is almost never ignorance of a component — it is answering a question nobody asked, at a level of detail nobody wanted, having never established what the thing has to do
beats.fix: spend the first minutes establishing scale, traffic shape and what must not fail, then state the simplest design that meets it, then break it deliberately and repair what broke
beats.cost: establishing scope costs time that feels like not answering, and the numbers you commit to early constrain everything afterwards — which is the point, and is uncomfortable
beats.interview: how to open when the question is deliberately vague
